text:
cheng: Noticing weird head-of-line blocking in us-west-2 GPU pool — some gpus at 95% and many GPUs sitting idle. Jobs are queued but not dispatched evenly. Anyone else seeing uneven utilization?

maria: Yep saw alerts. Which pool/name? can you paste the admission controller logs? :thinking_face:

cheng: pool: gpu-pool-a. Attaching a short excerpt from admission logs and pod distribution.

dave: ```
# kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | egrep "gpu-pool-a|Pending"
inference-serve-7f5d   Running   1/1   4Gi   node-a-12   10.0.2.34   gpu:1
inference-serve-9c2a   Pending   0/1   4Gi   -           -           gpu:1 (waiting admission)
inference-batch-21kq   Running   1/1   4Gi   node-a-14   10.0.2.36   gpu:1
inference-batch-4zre   Pending   0/1   4Gi   -           -           gpu:1 (waiting admission)
```

There are many pending pods but they all seem pinned to a small set of nodes while other nodes have spare capacity.

elaine: Found a likely culprit in the admission controller math. When we compute per-shard allowance we do: `per_shard = floor(total_capacity / shard_count)` and then use `per_shard * shard_count` as the allowed inflight. If shard_count increases dynamically during autoscale the floor causes unallocated tokens that never get assigned — fragments the global capacity across shards.

elaine: Example excerpt from code (simplified):
```py
# admission.py
total = cluster_gpu_count()  # e.g., 48
shards = len(active_shards)  # e.g., 7
per_shard = total // shards  # floor division => 6
allowed = per_shard * shards  # 42, 6 GPUs effectively lost
```

cheng: That matches the symptom — effective capacity lost and requests stuck at head of per-shard queues while other shards had spare GPUs.

maria: Is there a quick mitigation we can apply without rolling full infra? Maybe enable a global pooling flag or bump burst tokens?

dave: I pushed a temporary patch to the admission controller to distribute the remainder tokens round-robin instead of dropping them. Patch diff: `remainder = total % shards; distribute(remainder)` — applied as a hotfix to us-west-2 canary.

infra-bot: deploy 1805432301 by dave to admission/us-west-2 succeeded in canary (1 pod).

cheng: After canary we see pending queue draining on the canary shard, but a couple of other shards still blocked. Need full rollout.

elaine: Long term fix: switch to a global admission queue with fair-share semantics and preemptible reservation for small latency-sensitive requests. Also we need unit tests for dynamic shard count and an integration test exercising autoscale+admission.

sre-oncall: Impact assessment — several production customers experienced 3-10s tail latency spikes for request creation and a cost bump from inefficient packing. No pod evictions, no node failures. SLA impact: transient but measurable.

maria: Plan: 1) finish rollout of remainder-distribution hotfix to all regions (rolling, low-risk) 2) telemetry: add metric `admission.unallocated_capacity` and alert if > 5% for >10m 3) backlog ticket for global-queue rework + tests.

dave: Rolling remainder hotfix to all regions now. ETA ~20m. Will post status.

cheng: Thx. After rollout we'll run a synthetic workload to validate even packing and watch GPU allocation heatmaps. Also adding a follow-up to postmortem with root cause + mitigation.

maria: Sounds good. @elaine can you open the ticket for the global-queue rework and link to this thread? :thumbsup: 

elaine: On it, will include code refs and test plan. Ticket created: INFRA-1248.

infra-bot: monitor alert cleared for us-west-2 admission queue at 1805432559.

cheng: Verified heatmap improved, pending pods drained. Closing loop once rollout completes everywhere. Thanks all.
